explanation: In C++, class templates allow defining generic classes that can operate with any data type. Operator overloading within class templates enables customizing how operators behave for specific template instantiations, providing intuitive and type-safe operations. Overloading operators like 'operator<=' for class templates such as std::array allows comparing objects of the template class in a natural way, leveraging C++'s powerful template system to write flexible, reusable code.
syntax:
template <class T, size_t N>
bool operator<=(const array<T,N>& x, const array<T,N>& y);
example_explanation: This example defines a template function to overload the '<=' operator for std::array objects of any type T and size N. It compares two arrays element-wise to determine if the first is less than or equal to the second. The main function creates two arrays and uses the overloaded operator to compare them, demonstrating how operator overloading in class templates enables intuitive comparison operations for generic container types in modern C++.
